title: Reciprocal zenith distances of the USC&GS Transcontinental Triangulation (Schott, Special Publication No. 4, 1900, Part II): Colorado, the California coast, Mount Hamilton, and Round Top-Jackson Butte hour by hour in 1879; our transcription
verdict_rule: Reciprocal zenith distances whose sums stay at or below 180°, whatever the length of the line (a plane with straight or downward-bent light).

sources.cite: C. A. Schott, The Transcontinental Triangulation and the American Arc of the Parallel, U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey Special Publication No. 4 (Washington, 1900), Part II, Determination of heights: pp. 257-262, 269-277, 280-292, 300-302 of the print (pdf pp. 261-307)

units.red_level, red_ecc: arcsec, Schott's reductions to the station mark and for eccentricity
units.P_mm, T_C: the abstracts' rough pressure (mm of mercury) and air temperature (°C)
units.log_s: log10 of the distance in metres, as printed

inputs.origin: Schott, USC&GS Special Publication No. 4 (1900), Part II (determination of heights), the pages named in the file name; typed by hand by the assistant (Claude) from the scans, under Xyphophor's review.
inputs.checks: The build checks observed + reductions = reduced, the means, and log s.

notes: The PDF is the one of surv-excess (data/surv/excess/sp4/raw/). 'component' rows are the years a 'mean' row combines; pairs use the mean. s/E = R/(1−k) is a measure (s from the triangulation, E from two angles); k needs R (check). Method: go doc -all ./internal/build/survzenith.
